chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the person in ihram carry weapons? He said: 'If the person in ihram fears an enemy or robbers, let him wear the weapons.' And there is no harm if a man disciplines his slave when he has need for that, while he is in ihram. Narrated.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim in ihram carry weapons for protection?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that carrying weapons (sillāḥ) does not invalidate the state of iḥram, provided the intent is protection from enemies or robbers, reflecting the practical flexibility of Shia fiqh in pilgrimage rituals. It further establishes the permissibility of disciplining a slave during iḥram, highlighting the continuity of domestic authority even in the sacred state. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on expiation (kaffārah) for unintentional violations of iḥram conditions.
